precepts.text: Captain: he removeth away the speech of the trusty, and taketh away the understanding of the aged. Just because you think you are wise in your older years, the Lord will take away your understanding, so no one should trust what an old fool says. Daniel's wisdom was called upon as a young man; Paul told Timothy to let no man despise his youth, a younger man who became an elder over the church. Many of the prophets were called young and set over congregations because the aged, who were supposed to have the wisdom, did not; they judged incorrectly, took bribes, and were engulfed in their lust like the elders in the history of Susanna. Our leaders here in Israel United in Christ have proven themselves through time and through the rigorous scriptures, and that is why we give them the honor they deserve.
precepts.point: But wisdom is the gray hair unto men, and an unspotted life is old age. There is a reason the Messiah called you in your old age so the younger men can teach you; some of you in your old age are no good, your mind is gone, and the Messiah sent the young men to help you. Instead of embracing it you say, you cannot teach me anything. Then you are going to die in your sin, brother.
precepts.why:
We are supposed to learn from the aged. But as Wisdom of Solomon 4 says, honourable age is “not that which standeth in length of time, nor that is measured by number of years”, and Job shows why: “He removeth away the speech of the trusty, and taketh away the understanding of the aged.”

Look how the Lord deals. Just because you think you are wise in your older years, he will take away your understanding, so that no one should trust in what an old fool says. Our people think that because you are up in age you automatically get the respect. It is not about the age. It is about the wisdom the Lord placed in you, and the Lord can remove that from you.

That is why Daniel's wisdom was called upon while he was a young man, and why Paul instructed Timothy not to let anyone despise his youth: he was a younger man who became an elder over the church. Many of the prophets were called young and set over congregations to lead the people, because the aged, who were supposed to have the wisdom, did not. They were judging incorrectly, they were in briberies, and like the elders in the history of Susanna they were engulfed in their lust. So the Lord called younger men to do what the older men were not doing.

So “wisdom is the gray hair unto men, and an unspotted life is old age.” There is a reason the Messiah called you in your old age so the younger men can teach you. If instead of embracing it you say, I'm too old for these young men to tell me what to do, you cannot teach me nothing, you are going to die in your sin, brother. Our leaders in Israel United in Christ have proven themselves through time and through the rigorous scriptures, and have applied them, and that is why we give them the honor they deserve.

precepts.text: The bewitching of naughtiness doth obscure things that are honest.
precepts.point: The Lord set a mark on Cain lest any should kill him. The mark is sin, which preserves the wicked until their judgment.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
Why would a mark of sin protect Cain? Solomon answers: “For the bewitching of naughtiness doth obscure things that are honest; and the wandering of concupiscence doth undermine the simple mind.” Sin is bewitching. It is seductive. It hides what is honest, so that, as the scripture says, if it were possible even the elect would be deceived.

That is how the mark works. Cain’s line would have rulership for a time, and he would rule the earth with darkness, with sin and with evil, and people would be enticed by it, Israelites included. Our northern kingdom, the majority of it, fell for it, and now they are getting their wake-up call, though there was always a remnant that rebelled against the colonialism they saw in Latin America.

The bewitching is also how the confederacy holds together. The other nations know what he stands for; it is common knowledge. But the love of money, power and rulership says, put that aside, this is the one it was given to, nobody else could get me these things. So they ally with him, and there is no honor among thieves with this man. We watch him boast of taking Venezuela’s president in an operation so fast and violent, threaten the vice president with worse, and name Colombia and Mexico next.

But the spell does not last. “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” We know who brings him down: first those he dealt with turn against him, and then Christ and his elect have the glory and honor of taking him down. The wicked are revealed and restrained for a time, a hedge around them until they fulfill what the Lord wants, and then comes their final judgment.

precepts.text: His grace and mercy is with his saints, and he hath respect unto his chosen.
precepts.point: Respect unto His chosen is not respect of persons. Within Israel there is no respect of persons: the Most High renders to every man according to his deeds, tribulation and anguish upon every soul that doeth evil, of the Jew first and also of the Gentile, the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom that was Hellenized; but glory, honour, and peace to every man that worketh good. The nation is chosen above the nations, and all Israel shall be saved through the Deliverer out of Sion.
precepts.why:
“This the people saw, and understood it not, neither laid they up this in their minds, That his grace and mercy is with his saints, and that he hath respect unto his chosen.”

God had respect unto the children of Israel because he hath respect unto his chosen. His grace and mercy is with his saints. The people saw it and did not understand it, but it is written plainly here: the respect God shows is to his chosen.

precepts.text: The gray head is a good name kept blameless.
precepts.point: The blueness of a wound cleanses away evil, and so do stripes the inward parts of the belly; the older generation knows well what that discipline meant.

note.label: Proverbs 20: Integrity, Just Weights, and Waiting on the Lord

precepts.why:
“The glory of young men is their strength: and the beauty of old men is the gray head.” The gray head is a beauty, but not simply because of the years behind it.

Wisdom of Solomon says what honorable age really is: “For honourable age is not that which standeth in length of time, nor that is measured by number of years.” Honorable age is not length of years but wisdom; the gray hair is an unspotted life and a good name kept blameless. A man can be old and have none of that beauty, and that gray head is only years.

So the beauty of old men is a life kept clean and a name kept blameless, the wisdom that the years were supposed to bring. That is the gray head Solomon calls beautiful.

precepts.text: His grace and mercy is with his saints, and that he hath respect unto his chosen.
precepts.point: Moses gave the first covenant; grace and truth are the new one. Where the law of Moses required a man's own blood for certain things, there is now a mediator.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
Solomon says it a second time: “This the people saw, and understood it not, neither laid they up this in their minds, That his grace and mercy is with his saints, and that he hath respect unto his chosen.”

His grace and mercy is with his saints, and he has respect unto his chosen. The people saw it and understood it not, and did not lay it up in their minds. So when John says “grace and truth came by Jesus Christ”, that grace is with the saints, his chosen, the ones he has respect unto.
